title: Turn-prognosis driven KV reservation and slab-smoothing for continuous batcher
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: For mixed prompt/response lengths our continuous batcher is oscillating between over-reserving KV for occasional long turns (causing GPU slab fragmentation and higher tail latency) and under-reserving (causing evictions and repeated recomputation). Existing heuristics use static length thresholds and simple LRU-based KV eviction which doesn't account for imminent long continuations from the same session or user pattern.

Goal: Implement a light-weight 'turn-prognosis' signal into the scheduler that predicts, at request admission time, the probability that the current stream will require a long continuation (long response or long next user turn). Use that probability to drive a soft KV-reservation budget, speculative KV warm-up, and a slab-smoothing policy that staggers reclamation to reduce fragmentation bursts. Primary success metrics are reduced KV eviction-rate, lower GPU memory variance across windows, and no regression to P95 latency or throughput.

Scope: Prototype model + scheduler integration, simulator evaluation, canary rollout on low-traffic pools, metrics instrumentation, and playbook for rollback. Not in scope: full retraining pipeline for the prognostic model (we will use lightweight online-updatable model and a simple feature set).
acceptance_criteria: Turn-prognosis model < 5KB per-instance and <0.5ms avg inference on CPU
Scheduler consumes turn-prognosis probability to set per-slot soft-reservation (0..1) and respects global GPU memory SLOs
KV eviction rate decreased by >=15% in simulator for mixed-turn workloads compared to baseline
GPU slab fragmentation metric (slab-variance) reduced by >=20% over 60s windows in canary
No increase in P95 generation latency >5ms at 95% confidence during canary (5% traffic)
design_notes: Turn-prognosis signal: simple logistic model trained offline on turn-history features (token_count,last_response_length,inter-arrival-ms,user-cohort,dialogue-position). Model persisted as small weights and evaluated in the scheduler admission path.

Soft-reservation: Instead of hard pinning KV pages, assign a reservation score R in [0,1] per slot derived from probability p: R = clamp(alpha * p + beta * recent_slot_stability, 0,1). Reservation increments influence prefetch budget and eviction priority (lower priority for reserved slots).

Slab-smoothing: Add a 'cooldown window' per slab region. When reservation increases, instead of immediate eviction we schedule staggered reclamation across slabs to avoid large contiguous free/used churn which causes fragmentation on next allocations.
Speculative warm-up: For high p slots we do asynchronous KV warm-up of likely prefix tokens using low-priority background workers with strict token and time budgets to cap cost.

Fallbacks: If overall GPU memory pressure is high, reservations are honored probabilistically (global throttle) and speculative warm-up is paused. We maintain existing eviction policies as ultimate fallback.
Metrics: add kv_eviction_rate, kv_prefetch_cost_tokens, slab_variance (per-GPU), reservation_hit_rate, turn_prognosis_auc, warmup_success_rate. Instrument at token-level and slot-level for tracing.
Privacy: Model features exclude raw user content; only length/timing/cohort metadata used. No PII stored in training features.
progress_updates: 2025-01-10 - Triage: scoped POC. Decided to prioritize a tiny model evaluated inline on the scheduler host to avoid RPC overhead.

2025-01-15 - Design review with runtime team. Raised trade-offs: reservation reduces evictions but can increase transient memory pressure; agreed to implement global throttle and soft-reservation semantics.

2025-01-22 - POC model implemented using logistic regression (scikit-like impl) and integrated into simulator. Initial sim on synthetic mixlen trace shows 18% eviction reduction and 12% slab_variance improvement.

2025-01-28 - Prototype scheduler change committed to branch 'eng/turn-prognosis'. Added flags: turn_prognosis_enable, reservation_alpha/beta, slab_cooldown_ms. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12841
2025-02-02 - Canary plan approved: 5% traffic on pool-beta for 48h, shadow mode for 24h before soak. Dashboard template created. Linked confluence doc and runbook.
2025-02-05 - Baseline metrics captured and canary kickoff scheduled for 2025-02-07. Added additional trace points for per-slot reservation reasons.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Mis-calibrated model causes over-reservation -> OOM or eviction ripple. Mitigation: global memory throttle and automatic pause when slab_variance or gpu_free drops below threshold.
Risk: Warm-up cost increases token bill. Mitigation: strict warm-up token budget per-minute and cost-tracking metric; can be disabled remotely.
Risk: Model drift over time. Mitigation: collect lightweight labeled stream for periodic re-calibration and add A/B to compare static heuristic baseline.

Risk: Scheduler latency increase from extra decisioning. Mitigation: keep model <0.5ms CPU inference, micro-benchmarking done; fall back to cached last-prognosis for repeat requests from same session.
Rollbacks: toggle turn_prognosis_enable=false or set reservation_alpha=0 to instantly revert behavior.
tests: Unit tests for reservation math and slab cooldown scheduler (CI)
Simulator integration tests using real mixlen traces (stored in s3://redwood-test-data/mixlen-traces)
Canary e2e: 48h canary with P95 latency, kv_eviction_rate, slab_variance and cost dashboards monitored
Load test: synthetic spike with 10x long-turn fraction to validate graceful degradation and global throttle
